Sirvydis was selected 37th overall by the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in the [[2019 NBA draft]] and was then traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]]. ==Early life and youth career== Sirvydis spent his childhood in various European countries because of his father's professional basketball career. He lived for three years in [[Russia]], two years in [[Germany]], one year in the [[Czech Republic]], and one year in [[Cyprus]]. Sirvydis often practiced basketball after his father's games but did not seriously start playing the sport until he was about seven years old.{{cite web |last1=Hein |first1=David |title=Sirvydis keeps etching his name in annals of Rytas history |url=https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/8hoewki9ubhwv7fs/sirvydis-keeps-etching-his-name-in-annals-of-rytas-history |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] |access-date=10 May 2019 |date=24 January 2018}} In May 2018, Sirvydis won the [[2017–18 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|2017–18 Adidas Next Generation Tournament]] with the [[BC Rytas|Rytas Vilnius]] U18 team and was named [[most valuable player]] after recording 18 points, 6 rebounds and 3 assists in the title game against [[A.S. Stella Azzurra|Stella Azzurra Rome]] under-18 team.{{cite web |title=Rytas guard Sirvydis named ANGT MVP |url=https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/8r35meqnjihofupj/rytas-guard-sirvydis-named-angt-mvp |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] |access-date=10 May 2019 |date=20 May 2018}} ==Professional career== ===Rytas Vilnius (2017–2020)=== Sirvydis made his [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian Basketball League]] (LKL) debut with [[BC Rytas|Rytas Vilnius]] on 29 May 2017, at age 16, and passed [[Jonas Valančiūnas]] as the youngest player in club history to play in the league. On 5 December, he became the youngest Lietuvos rytas player to appear in a [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] game, overtaking Valančiūnas again. In the 2019–20 season, Sirvydis averaged 6.6 points and 2.8 rebounds for Rytas in [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] play. He averaged 5.7 points and 2.5 rebounds per game in the LKL.{{cite web |title=Deividas Sirvydis palieka "Rytą" |url=https://basketnews.lt/news-139304-deividas-sirvydis-palieka-ryta.html |publisher=Basketnews |access-date=23 May 2020 |language=lt-LT}} ===Hapoel Jerusalem (2020)=== On 23 May 2020, Sirvydis signed a long-term contract with [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{cite web |title=Hapoel Jerusalem signs Deividas Sirvydis to long-term contract |date=23 May 2020 |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/fiba-champions-league/1062633/hapoel-jerusalem-signs-deividas-sirvydis-to-long-term-contract/ |publisher=EuroHoops |access-date=23 May 2020}} He left the team on 16 November to join the [[Detroit Pistons]] for training camp.{{cite news |last1=Williams |first1=Lauren |title=Pistons' 2019 pick Deividas Sirvydis reportedly joining team in training camp |url=https://www.mlive.com/pistons/2020/11/pistons-2019-pick-deividas-sirvydis-reportedly-joining-team-in-training-camp.html |access-date=17 November 2020 |work=[[MLive]] |date=16 November 2020}} ===Detroit Pistons / Motor City Cruise (2020–2022)=== In the [[2019 NBA draft]], Sirvydis was selected 37th overall by the [[Dallas Mavericks]], but was immediately traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in exchange for [[Isaiah Roby]] and two future second-round picks.{{cite web |title=Jaudinanti NBA naujokų birža: D.Sirvydis – į Detroitą, I.Brazdeikis – į Niujorką 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=27 June 2019}} He represented the Pistons at [[2019 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web |title=Su "Pistons" apranga debiutavęs D.Sirvydis nesikrimto dėl minučių: "Nerealus |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-free-agents-mason-plumlee-jahlil-okafor-josh-jackson-and-deividas-sirvydis |website=NBA.com |access-date=2 December 2020 |date=1 December |date=1 December 2020}} On 6 January 2021, Sirvydis made his the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) debut in a game against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web |title=Deividas Sirvydis debiutavo Sirvydis scored a career high of 16 points in a loss against the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|first=Omari|last=Sankofa II|title=Shorthanded Detroit Pistons fall to Nikola Jokic, Denver Nuggets at 2021|access-date=1 August 2021}} On 28 September, he re-signed with the Pistons,{{cite tweet|author=Pistons PR|number=1442865457237671939|title=The Detroit Pistons announced today that the team has Cruise Announce 2021-22 Training Camp Roster|url=https://detroit.gleague.nba.com/news/motor-city-cruise-announce-2021-22-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=25 October 2021|access-date=15 November 2021}} On 26 December 2021, the Pistons signed Sirvydis to a 10-day contract.{{cite tweet |user=Pistons_PR |number=1475223121493905408 |date=26 December 2021 |title=The #Pistons announced today that the club has signed Deividas Sirvydis to a 10-day contract using the COVID-related hardship allowance. Per team policy, terms of the agreement were not disclosed. |access-date=28 December 2021}}{{cite web |last1=Williams |first1=Lauren |title=Pistons sign Deividas Sirvydis to 10-day hardship contract |url=https://www.mlive.com/pistons/2021/12/pistons-sign-deividas-sirvydis-to-10-day-hardship-contract.html |website=mlive |access-date=28 December 2021 |date=26 December 2021}} Sirvydis was assigned to the Cruise on 5 January 2022.{{cite news |title=Deividas Sirvydis: Short-term contract expires |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/deividas-sirvydis-short-term-contract-expires/ |access-date=6 January 2022 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=5 January 2022}} After his 10-day contract with the Pistons expired, Sirvydis returned to the Cruise. On February 17, 2022, Sirvydis set the Motor City Cruise record for Most 3-pointers made in a single game when he made 7 of his 14 attempts and had totals of 25 points and 7 rebounds as the Cruise defeated the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] 132 - 120.{{cite web | title=FWN vs MCC | url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/game/2022100282/ }} Sirvydis joined the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |title=New Orleans Pelicans 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612740/pelicans |access-date=July 5, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} On 18 August 2022, he signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web |title=Pacers Sign Deividas Sirvydis |url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-deividas-sirvydis |website=NBA.com |access-date=30 September 2022 |date=18 August 2022}} On 22 October, the Pacers waived Sirvydis before the beginning of the regular season.{{cite web |title=Indiana Pacers Announce Roster Moves |url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-announce-roster-moves-221014 |website=NBA.com |access-date=18 October 2022}} ===Fort Wayne Mad Ants (2022–2023)=== On 24 October 2022, Sirvydis joined the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] training camp roster.{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/mad-ants-announce-2022-training-camp-roster/n-5892665|website=oursportscentral.com|title=Mad Ants Announce 2022 Training Camp Roster|date=October 24, 2022|access-date=October 24, 2022}} ===Wisconsin Herd (2023)=== On 24 February 2023, Sirvydis was traded to the [[Wisconsin Herd]] in exchange for [[Jordan Bone]].{{Cite magazine |title=Fort Wayne Mad Ants acquire two former NBA players in recent moves, trade away former Pacer Deividas Sirvydis |url=https://www.si.com/nba/pacers/roster/fort-wayne-mad-ants-acquire-two-former-nba-players-recent-moves-trade-away-pacers-deividas-sirvydis |access-date=February 25, 2023 |magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=25 February 2023 }} ===Lietkabelis Panevėžys (2023–2024)=== On 3 August 2023, Sirvydis returned to Europe, signing with [[BC Lietkabelis|7bet-Lietkabelis Panevėžys]] of the [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian Basketball League]] (LKL) and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]. The contract included EuroLeague and NBA opt-out clauses.{{cite web|title=Deividas Sirvydis returns to Europe, keeps EuroLeague option open|url=https://basketnews.com/news-192827-deividas-sirvydis-returns-to-europe-keeps-euroleague-option-open.html|website=BasketNews.com|date=3 August 2023|access-date=4 August 2023}}{{cite web|title="7bet-Lietkabelyje" – į Europą rungtyniauti grįžtantis Deividas Sirvydis|url=https://www.kklietkabelis.lt/7bet-lietkabelyje-i-europa-rungtyniauti-griztantis-deividas-sirvydis/|website=KKLietkabelis.lt|date=3 August 2023|access-date=4 August 2023|language=lt}} In the [[2023–24 EuroCup Basketball|2023–24 EuroCup]] season he became the highest average scoring player in the league, averaging 18.9 points. ===Žalgiris Kaunas (2024–present)=== On 18 June 2024,
